item.title: Ise Jingu Geku: The Outer Shrine of Ise — Guide
item.description: The Geku (Outer Shrine) of Ise Jingu is where a proper pilgrimage to Ise begins, as tradition dictates it be visited before the Naiku. It enshrines Toyouke-Omikami, the goddess of agriculture, food and industry, who was summoned some 1,500 years ago to provide sacred meals to the sun goddess Amaterasu at the Inner Shrine — a duty still performed twice daily. Its unpainted hinoki halls, in the same austere ancient style as the Naiku and likewise rebuilt every 20 years, sit within a hushed forest just a short walk from Ise-shi Station, making it the natural first stop.

item.title: Ise Jingu Complete Guide: Japan's Most Sacred Shrine
item.description: Ise Jingu stands apart from every other sacred site in Japan. Not by scale — there are shrine complexes that cover more ground — but by the nature of its significance. For over 2,000 years, Ise has been the spiritual centre of the Japanese nation, the home of Amaterasu Omikami, the sun goddess from whom the imperial family traces its divine lineage. The Emperor of Japan makes a personal visit to Ise at the beginning of each reign.
